cohort: Women with singleton gestations and a history of three or more prior cesarean deliveries who delivered at one of two urban tertiary care hospitals, one with a policy of 37-week delivery and the other with a policy of 39-week delivery for higher order cesarean sections
finding: While a policy of planned delivery at 37 weeks was associated with a reduction in unscheduled deliveries, there were no significant differences in perinatal outcomes after controlling for potential confounders.
mod_finding: A policy of planned delivery at 37 weeks for women undergoing a higher order cesarean was associated with a reduction in unscheduled deliveries, but no significant differences in perinatal outcomes compared to planned delivery at 39 weeks.
